def factor_tail_semivariance_asymmetry(df):
    """Measures downside variance dominance as a stress accumulation proxy; higher values indicate heavier lower tail."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    down_ret = ret.where(ret < 0)
    up_ret = ret.where(ret > 0)
    down_var = (down_ret ** 2).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    up_var = (up_ret ** 2).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    factor = down_var / up_var.replace(0, np.nan)
    factor = factor.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    df_copy["factor_tail_semivariance_asymmetry"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_tail_semivariance_asymmetry"]
description: The factor computes the ratio of rolling 60-day downside variance to upside variance. Higher downside variance relative to upside variance indicates asymmetric lower-tail risk and stress accumulation. This uncovered pathway directly measures variance asymmetry rather than skew/kurtosis or return percentiles, enriching tail-risk detection.
